source_text: συναντῆσαι αὐτοὺς ὑμῖν μετὰ ἄρτων καὶ ὕδατος ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἐκπορευομένων ὑμῶν ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ὅτι ἐμισθώσαντο ἐπὶ σὲ τὸν Βαλαὰμ υἱὸν Βεὼρ ἐκ τῆς Μεσοποταμίας καταρᾶσθαί σε. Καὶ οὐκ ἠθέλησε Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου εἰσακοῦσαι τοῦ Βαλαὰμ, καὶ μετέστρεψε Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου τὰς κατάρας εἰς εὐλογίαν, ὅτι ἠγάπησέ σε Κύριος ὁ Θεός σου. Οὐ προσαγορεύσεις εἰρηνικὰ αὐτοῖς, καὶ συμφέροντα αὐτοῖς, πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας σου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τίς ἂν νοοῖτο θλαδίας καὶ ἀποκεκομμένος, Ἀμμανίτης καὶ Μωαβίτης, ἐθέλοιμ' ἂν ἐκμαθεῖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄκουε δή· ὁ τῆς τῶν εὐνούχων ποιήσεως οὐχ εἶς τρόπος, οὐχ εἷς, ὦ Παλλάδιε, διττὸς δέ τις εἶναι λέγεται, καὶ πεφώραται. Οἱ μὲν γάρ εἰσι τομίαι καὶ διεσπασμένοι τὰ ἀρσενικά· οἱ δὲ τεθλασμένα καὶ ἀχρεῖα παντελῶς φέρουσιν ἔτι, ὠμῶς δὲ καὶ ἀνοσίως ἀποτέμνονταί τινες ἔσθ' ὅτε τὸ παιδοποιὸν τοῦ σώματος μόριον, καί εἰσιν ἄπρακτοι πρὸς τὰ ἀνδρὸς, καίτοι τελοῦντες ἐν ἀνδράσι φύσει τε καὶ ἡλικίᾳ· ἀνδρείας δὲ σύμβολον, τὰ ἀρσενικά. Τὸν τοίνυν θλαδίαν ὑποτοπητέον, τὸν οἱονείπως οὐκ ἐξεσπασμένον εἰσάπαν ψυχήν τε καὶ νοῦν, συντεθραυσμένην δὲ μᾶλλον σώζοντά πως ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς ἀνδρίαν, ἀποκεκομμένον γε μὴν, τὸν ὁλοκλήρως αὐτὰ ἀποβεβληκότα, καὶ τῶν ἀνδράσι πρεπωδεστάτων ἐστερημένον. Ἐν ἴσῳ δὲ ὥσπερ ἐγκλήματι, τῷ μηδ' ὅλως ἀνδρίζεσθαι θέλειν, τὸ μὴ ὑγιῶς ἀνδρίζεσθαι φιλεῖν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οἷον δὴ τί φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀναπεπτώκασί τινες εἰς ἐπιθυμίας σαρκικὰς, ὅλας ὥσπερ ἡνίας ἀνέντες τῷ πάθει, σαθρόν τε καὶ ἄνανδρον ταῖς εἰς ἀσέλγειαν ἡδοναῖς παραῤῥιπτοῦντες τὸν νοῦν. Ἕτεροι δὲ αὖ θαυμάζουσι τὴν ἐγκράτειαν, καὶ ἅπτονται μὲν ἔσθ' ὅτε τῶν εἰς τοῦτο λαμπρῶν ἐπιχειρημάτων, ἐκδεδίασι δὲ τὴν ἀντίστασιν, καὶ τὴν τῆς ἡδονῆς προσβολὴν οὐ φέροντες, κατανύουσι πρὸς τὸ ἄναλκι. Ἆρ' οὖν, οὐχὶ τὸν μὲν εἰσάπαν ἀπειρηκότα τοῖς εἰς ἀνδρίαν ἐπιχειρήμασιν προσερεῖς εἰκότως ἀποκεκομμένον; Τὸν δὲ εἰς νοῦν μὲν ἔχοντα τὸ θέλειν ἀνδρίζεσθαι, μὴ μὴν ἔτι καὶ κατορθοῦν ἰσχύοντα τὴν ἀρετὴν, οἰήσῃ θλαδίαν, εἰς τρόπων ποιότητα μεταχαράττων ἀστείως καὶ τὰ τοῦ σώματος πάθη, καὶ εἰκόνα τῶν νοητῶν καὶ ἀφανεστέρων, τὰ ἐν αἰσθήσει δεχόμενος; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Συνεξείργετο δὲ τούτοις Ἀμμανίτης τε καὶ Μωαβίτης, ὡς ἀνόσιοί τε καὶ βδελυρώτατοι, καὶ λεόντων δίκην τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐπιφυόμενοι, καὶ τοῖς εὐδοκιμεῖν εἰωθόσι, τὰ ἐκ φθόνου καὶ βασκανίας ἐπιχέοντες βέλη. Τύπος δ' ἂν εἶεν, Ἀμμανῖται μὲν δὴ, τῶν ἀφιλοικτιρμόνων αἱρετικῶν. Μωαβῖται δὲ αὖ, τῶν ἐν πλάναις ἔτι ταῖς εἰδωλικαῖς, καὶ ταῖς τῶν δαιμονίων μοχθηρίαις ὑπεστρωμένων· θεοστυγεῖς γὰρ ἄμφω, καὶ ἀδελφὸν ὥσπερ κατὰ τῶν ἁγίων νοσοῦντες τὸ θράσος.
pass_a_gloss: Cyril (cont. of Deuteronomy): …meet you with breads and water on the way, as you were going out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia to curse you. And the Lord your God was not willing to hearken to Balaam, and the Lord your God turned the curses into blessing, because the Lord your God loved you. You shall not address peaceful things to them and advantageous things to them all your days forever.' Palladius: And who would be understood [as] crushed and cut-off, Ammonite and Moabite, I would wish to learn thoroughly. Cyril: Hear then: the manner of the making of eunuchs is not one, not one, O Palladius, but it is said to be some twofold, and has been detected. For some are cut and torn apart as to the male parts; and others still bear [them] crushed and altogether useless; and sometimes some cruelly and impiously have cut off (mid. pass) the child-making part of the body, and they are ineffective for the things of a man, although being numbered among men by nature and age; and the male parts [are] a symbol of manliness/courage. The crushed one, then, must be supposed [to be] the one as it were not wholly torn out in soul and mind, but rather somehow preserving in himself, shattered, the manliness for good things; and the cut-off one, the one who has wholly cast away them and been deprived of the things most befitting men. As in an equal charge, with not wishing to play the man at all, [is] to be fond of playing the man not soundly. Palladius: Such as what do you say? Cyril: Some have fallen back into fleshly desires, letting go as it were the whole reins to the passion, throwing aside the mind, rotten and unmanly, to the pleasures toward licentiousness. And others again admire self-control, and sometimes take hold of the splendid attempts toward this, but they dread the resistance, and not bearing the attack of pleasure, they end up in feebleness. Will you not then reasonably address the one who has altogether given up on the attempts toward manliness as cut off? And the one having in mind the willing to play the man, but not also being able to accomplish virtue, will you think crushed, re-stamping wittily even the body's afflictions into quality of ways/character, and receiving the things in sense-perception as image of the intelligible and more hidden? Palladius: Certainly. Cyril: And together with these were shut out Ammonite and Moabite, as unholy and most loathsome, and like lions attacking the saints, and pouring on those accustomed to be well regarded the darts of envy and malice. They would be a type: the Ammonites of the pitiless heretics; the Moabites, of those still laid under the idolatrous errors and the wickednesses of the demons; for both [are] God-hated, and sick with a brother-like boldness against the saints.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …meet you with bread and water on the way when you were coming out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia against you, to curse you. But the Lord your God would not listen to Balaam, and the Lord your God turned the curses into a blessing, because the Lord your God loved you. You shall not speak words of peace to them, or words for their good, all your days forever’ (Deuteronomy 23:4–6).
Palladius: I should like to learn who is to be understood by the crushed and the cut off, the Ammonite and the Moabite.

Cyril: Listen, then. Eunuchs are not made in one way only, not one, Palladius; there are said to be two ways, and so it has been found. Some are castrated, with the male parts torn away; others still have them, but crushed and wholly useless. And sometimes people cruelly and impiously have the part of the body that begets children cut off, and they are incapable of a man’s functions, even though by nature and age they are counted among men. Now the male parts are a symbol of manly courage. We must take the crushed man, then, to be the one who has not, so to speak, been wholly torn away in soul and mind, but rather keeps somehow within himself his courage for what is good, though it is shattered; and the man cut off to be the one who has thrown these away entirely and been deprived of what most befits men. And to love a courage that is not sound stands, as it were, under the same charge as not wishing to be brave at all.

Cyril: Some have slumped into fleshly desires, letting go of the reins entirely, as it were, to passion, and they cast their mind, rotten and unmanly, before the pleasures of licentiousness. Others, again, admire self-control, and sometimes take up splendid efforts toward it, but they dread the struggle and, unable to bear the onslaught of pleasure, end in weakness. Will you not, then, rightly call the one who has wholly given up efforts toward courage cut off? And will you not think the one who has in mind the will to be brave, yet is not also able to achieve virtue, crushed, neatly recasting even the body’s afflictions as qualities of character, and taking what is perceived by the senses as an image of things grasped by the mind and more hidden?

Cyril: Along with these, the Ammonite and the Moabite were shut out too, as unholy and utterly loathsome, men who set upon the saints like lions and pour out the arrows of envy and spite on those who are held in good repute. The Ammonites would be a type of the heretics, who know no pity; the Moabites, of those still lying under the errors of idolatry and the wickedness of demons. For both are hateful to God, and both are sick with a kindred boldness, as it were, against the saints.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 14 exists to compare. Translated fresh from the Migne PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: Migne PG 68 print; the column break may cut a sentence or a word.

Deuteronomy 23:4–6 in English numbering (LXX/Hebrew 23:5–7); it completes the quotation begun at the end of section 4. Cyril's text switches between plural 'you' (ὑμῖν) and singular (σέ) as LXX does; the English 'you' covers both. Οὐ προσαγορεύσεις εἰρηνικὰ αὐτοῖς καὶ συμφέροντα αὐτοῖς follows the LXX ('speak peace … and what is to their advantage'), not the Hebrew 'seek their peace'. Wordplay: ἀνδρεία/ἀνδρία (courage, literally 'manliness') with ἀνδρίζεσθαι ('to play the man') carries the eunuch figure; rendered 'manly courage', 'courage', 'be brave'. ἀποτέμνονταί τινες may be middle (some cut off their own member) or passive; the English 'have … cut off' allows both. τὸ μὴ ὑγιῶς ἀνδρίζεσθαι φιλεῖν rendered 'to love a courage that is not sound'. θεοστυγεῖς may mean 'hateful to God' or 'God-hating' (as in Romans 1:30); rendered 'hateful to God'. 'Like brothers' (ἀδελφὸν ὥσπερ … τὸ θράσος) plays on Ammon and Moab being brothers, sons of Lot's daughters (Genesis 19:36–38); uncited as a pun, not an allusion to the verse. 'Like lions' carries no clear Scripture reference here; uncited.
συντεθραυσμένην agrees with ἀνδρίαν: made 'shattered' clearly modify the courage; removed added 'still' (Greek μᾶλλον 'rather')
ἀδελφὸν ὥσπερ … τὸ θράσος was rendered twice ('like brothers' + 'kindred'); now once
